newsitem.title: CHINA: China Great Wall wants to list subsidiaries.
newsitem.headline: China Great Wall wants to list subsidiaries.

text.p: China Great Wall Industry Corp, a major state-run conglomerate, plans to list at least two of its subsidiaries on domestic stock exchanges in the medium term, a senior company official said on Thursday.
The company is reorganising subsidiaries in the southern city of Shenzhen and in central Xian in preparation for the move.
"We do not want to list the parent company but we are planning listings for some of our subsidiaries," Yang Xueming, general manager of the company's planning department, told Reuters.
Yang said in an interview that Great Wall was reorganising the subsidiaries as shareholding companies and would seek listings in one to two years.
Securities rules normally require a three-year track record as a shareholding company, the first step towards making a public offer.
"We want to see the process speeded up," he said without saying how the company would be able to cut the waiting period.
China has two domestic stock exchanges -- one in Shanghai and the other in Shenzhen.
Yang said the Xian operations, called Xian Aerospace Great Wall, included both foreign trade and high technology production, such as computer controls for electric power networks.
The Shenzhen company, Shenzhen Guangyu Industrial Group, operates a joint venture with Malaysian interests to manufacture air conditioners.
He did not give details of the value of the assets of either company or say how much the two offers might raise.
China Great Wall Industry, an arm of the state-run China Aerospace Corp, is a conglomerate that supplies missiles and is responsble for satellite launches for foreign companies.
It also trades or produces a wide range of civilian products and has interests in companies engaged in hotels, taxis, real estate and computers.
